text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand, which helps developers find and fix problems faster. When you refactor, you might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate logic. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly without attention to quality. By cleaning up code regularly, teams can keep their projects healthy and avoid bigger problems in the future.
